summary: Specifies the Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol, which lets PPP traffic be tunneled through an IP network. It is informational and not a standard.

plainLanguage.summary: The Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol (PPTP) carries Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) packets between a dial-access device and a network server through an Internet Protocol (IP) network. A Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connection manages calls, while an enhanced Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) tunnel carries user data.

questions: how does point to point tunneling work
what is a pac and pns in pptp
subtitle: Carries PPP sessions across IP using a TCP control connection and a GRE data tunnel.

tldr.problem: A network access server traditionally combines dial-line handling, PPP termination and network routing in one system. PPTP separates these functions so PPP sessions can be carried across an IP network.
tldr.mechanism: A PPTP Access Concentrator and a PPTP Network Server use a TCP control connection for calls and an enhanced GRE tunnel for PPP packets. The tunnel multiplexes sessions and uses acknowledgments for flow control, not retransmission.
tldr.outcome: PPTP carries PPP without changing PPP itself. RFC 2637 is Informational, and its IESG note says a vendor consortium developed it while the PPP working group was defining L2TP as a Standards Track protocol.

facts.label: Encapsulated user-data MTU
facts.value: 1532 octets, excluding IP and GRE headers

today: RFC 2637 is an Informational memo, not an Internet standard. Its IESG note says L2TP was being defined by the PPP working group as a Standards Track protocol.

sections.title: The PAC and PNS Roles
sections.content:
PPTP divides the traditional network access server functions between a PPTP Access Concentrator (PAC) and a PPTP Network Server (PNS). The PAC handles the PSTN or ISDN line and PPP link termination; the PNS handles functions such as PPP network control protocols, multilink bundles and routing.

The RFC says this separation can support flexible IP address management, tunnel non-IP protocols through an IP-only provider and distribute channels from a multilink bundle across several PACs. Only the PAC and PNS need to know about PPTP, and standard PPP client software should continue to work.
sections.plainLanguage: The PAC handles the phone or ISDN connection, while the PNS handles network functions. They carry the PPP session between them without changing the PPP protocol.

sections.title: Control Connection and Tunnel
sections.content:
Each PAC-PNS pair uses two parallel connections. The control connection is a TCP session that carries call setup, management and release messages. Either side may initiate it, and it uses TCP port 1723.

An IP tunnel between the same pair carries PPP packets inside enhanced GRE packets. A key in the GRE header identifies the session, so several sessions can share a tunnel. The control connection establishes and manages the sessions carried through it.
sections.plainLanguage: One connection carries instructions about calls. A separate tunnel carries the PPP packets for those calls, with a session identifier in each packet.

sections.title: Control Messages and GRE Packets
sections.content:
Each control message starts with an 8-octet fixed header containing its total length, a message type and the magic cookie 0x1A2B3C4D. The RFC defines control messages for starting and stopping connections, echo checks, incoming and outgoing calls, errors and PPP session control.

The enhanced GRE header carries the peer's Call ID, payload length and optional sequence and acknowledgment numbers. Its protocol type is 0x880B. Acknowledgments indicate which packets arrived and help regulate sending; they do not trigger retransmission of user data.
sections.plainLanguage: Control messages identify what connection or call action is requested. GRE packets identify which session carries each PPP packet and can acknowledge received packets.

sections.title: Call Setup and Connection Checks
sections.content:
A control connection must be established before PPTP messages can be exchanged. The peers send start requests and replies, check that they support a compatible version, and use echo messages to check that an established connection remains responsive. If a peer has received no control message for 60 seconds, it should send an Echo-Request; without a reply, it should close the connection after a further 60 seconds.

An incoming call uses a three-message exchange. The PAC reports the call, the PNS accepts or refuses it, and the PAC reports that the call connected. The PAC does not answer the telephone call before the PNS response. Call IDs identify sessions within a tunnel.
sections.plainLanguage: The PAC asks the PNS whether to accept an incoming call before answering it. Echo messages let the two systems check whether their control connection is still working.

sections.title: Flow Control and Packet Loss
sections.content:
The tunnel uses a sliding window to control how many unacknowledged packets a sender has in flight. The initial window is half the receiver's advertised maximum, with a minimum of one packet. It grows after acknowledged windows and shrinks after a timeout.

The tunnel does not retransmit GRE packets. A receiver must discard out-of-sequence packets or reorder them, because PPP handles loss but not reordered packets. The RFC suggests adaptive acknowledgment timeouts that increase after timeouts and decrease as acknowledgments arrive.
sections.plainLanguage: The sender adjusts how many packets it sends before waiting for acknowledgments. If packets arrive out of order, the receiver must reorder them or discard them; the tunnel does not resend lost user packets.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says PPP is responsible for protecting user data and authenticating PPP peers. PPTP control messages are not authenticated or integrity-protected, so they may be forged or changed in transit.

The GRE tunnel is not cryptographically protected. An attacker may observe or alter PPP negotiation carried through it. Unless the PPP payload is cryptographically protected, it can be captured, read or modified.
sections.plainLanguage: PPTP does not encrypt or authenticate its control messages or GRE tunnel. PPP data needs its own cryptographic protection if it must remain private and unchanged.
